question: Do the capability-writeback (capset) and non-blocking epoll_wait families, with no existing corpus guest, hold byte-identical parity under e9patch preprocessing with the golden hermit ptrace backend, after dropping keyctl which hermit does not support?
backend: ptrace (golden reference); e9patch = binary-rewriting preprocessing, not a backend
determinism_level: L2 (--strict --verify, guest-visible bitwise-identical; detlog tail-match modulo 8-syscall e9loader prologue)
dropped: keyctl_keyring_id: keyctl(250) KEYCTL_GET_KEYRING_ID returns failure under hermit (no usable kernel keyring)
host_independence: prints only syscall return on success (0) or a boolean; keyring id / capability bits read but not printed
gating: non-gated: capability writeback and non-blocking epoll_wait touch neither time, randomness, nor CPU scheduling; routine backend-parity, no post-facto-human-review trigger
ci_note: e9tool/e9patch absent from CI (like KVM /dev/kvm); corpus harness ungated, only audit-inventory gates these files
note: field thinning: rising drop rate across rounds (r22 0/6, r23 1/7, r24 4/7, r25 1/3); readily-reachable supported non-gated syscall families nearly exhausted. Confirmed hermit-unsupported this session: sched_getattr=275, io_setup=206, openat2=437, SysV IPC shmget=29/semget=64/msgget=68, keyctl=250. xattr write/get/remove on memfd fails natively (-EACCES/-ENODATA, tmpfs anon inode rejects user.* xattrs) so not shippable as host-independent success guests.
